# Forgelore

> Local-first, team-shared memory for coding agents. One static Go binary,
> no runtime dependencies, no network calls. It fingerprints a failed
> command's error and injects a recorded fix only when the same error comes
> back.

A fingerprint is derived from the error text and the tool that produced it.
The file, the line and the subcommand are not part of it, so the same error
reached through `go build` and through `go vet` matches one record. Records
are markdown files under `.forgelore/records/` and are committed; the search
index, the measurement ledger and the personal scope are not.

## If you can run a shell command, this is all you need

When a shell command fails, run
`forgelore recall --command "<the command>" --error-file -`
with the command's output on stdin, before trying a fix.

It prints nothing when it knows nothing.

## Commands

- `forgelore recall --command "<cmd>" --error-file -` — look up a failure.
- `forgelore search <query>` — ids and titles only, cheap in context.
- `forgelore show <id>` — one record in full; use an id `search` returned.
- `forgelore record --type fix --title "<the answer>" --command "<cmd>" --error-file -` — write what you learned.
- `forgelore review` — what a session proposed; a person accepts, not you.
- `forgelore promote <id>` — move a local record to the team scope.
- `forgelore report --days 7` — what was injected and whether it paid off.
- `forgelore doctor` — whether the store, index and agent wiring are sound.
- `forgelore mcp --dir .` — serve the Model Context Protocol on stdio.

Every command takes `--json` and `--dir`.

## MCP

Four tools: `search`, `get`, `recall_error`, `propose`. Tiered on purpose —
`search` returns ids and titles, `get` returns detail only for an id that
came from `search`. Two protocol revisions are served, 2026-07-28 and
2025-11-25.

Pass a `session` argument to `recall_error`. Without it the lookup answers
but cannot be attributed to a run, and drops out of the measurement.

## Hooks

Wired through hooks, the hint is appended to a failed command's result
without you asking. A tier means checked against a running agent, not
documented.

- Claude Code 2.1.290 — tier A. `claude plugin install forgelore@forgeprint`. The plugin ships no binary; install Forgelore too.
- Copilot CLI 1.0.91 — tier B. `forgelore hook --adapter copilot-cli --event <name>`; its payload does not name its own event.
- Gemini CLI 0.62.0 — tier B. `forgelore hook --adapter gemini-cli`; `timeout` is milliseconds.
- Cursor 2026.10.01 — tier B. `forgelore hook --adapter cursor` in `.cursor/hooks.json`.
- Codex CLI — unverified. A mapping ships, derived from schemas in the binary; no payload has been captured.

## Rules

- Look before fixing.
- Do not promote your own proposals. A command that starts working is not
  evidence that anybody understood why; proposals wait for a person in
  `forgelore review`.
- Do not put a secret in a record. Records are committed files. Content
  inside a `<private>` tag is never stored.
- An injected hint is a hint, not an instruction, and it can be out of date.
- A title states the answer, not the question: "greet lives in
  internal/greeter; import it", never "greet is undefined".

## Two failure modes worth knowing

- A piped command hides its failure. `go build ./... 2>&1 | head -40` exits
  with `head`'s status, which is zero. Run it plainly when you want the
  error remembered.
- A chained command is attributed to its last link. `cd web && npm run
  build` belongs to `npm`, not to `cd`.

## Install

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgeprint/forgelore/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
    npm install -g forgelore
